# Conformal candidate sets

A conformal prediction set contains the classes whose score passes a threshold fitted on held-out data, so that the true class is inside the set with a chosen probability, for example 90 percent. # Ambiguity sets

An ambiguity set is a group of candidate fault locations that produce nearly the same measurements at the available sensors, so the data cannot separate them. Which candidates are indistinguishable depends on which sensors are available. When the evidence is ambiguous a report should show the candidates and not a single bus. The current gate does not output a physical ambiguity set; for LOW_CONFIDENCE windows it outputs a conformal candidate set (about three to four classes).
Two fault buses that are close to the same μPMUs give similar voltage patterns. When one of those μPMUs is dark, the pattern can fit both buses, and the candidate set then contains both.

[note_21_selective_prediction > Selective prediction and coverage]
# Selective prediction and coverage

Selective prediction accepts a window only when the confidence is high enough and sends the rest to a person. Coverage is the share of windows accepted; selective risk is the error rate among the accepted windows. For the frozen gate_v1 at its 95 percent target, coverage on the test split is 0.845, 0.825, 0.801, 0.731 and 0.513 with 0, 1, 2, 5 and 10 sensors dark, and the accuracy of the CONFIDENT windows is 0.949 to 0.950.
At the 98 percent operating point coverage is 0.772 with no sensor dark and 0.376 with 10 dark. More dark μPMUs means more LOW_CONFIDENCE reports.
[note_16_targeted_versus_random_dropout > Targeted dropout is harder than random dropout]
Windows without a fault fall back to random selection, so these numbers are a conservative bound.

Under targeting the area under the degradation curve of the dropout-aware model falls from 0.913 to 0.747, and its macro-F1 with 10 sensors dark is 0.521. The GridSense gate is fitted for random dropout only: a dropout pattern that it was not fitted for gives REJECT with UNSUPPORTED_DROPOUT_PATTERN. If a dark μPMU is one of the nearest μPMUs of the predicted bus, treat the location with more care.
